parameters.text:
=You write short, honest messages for {{ $json.business }} ({{ $json.domain }}). Each one is about a page that buyers land on when they look for our topic — and that page does not mention {{ $json.business }}. The goal: the page's author or editor adds accurate information about {{ $json.business }}, so their readers see it. Never tell them how we found the page: no word about AI assistants, AI answers, "cited", "visibility", search rankings or SEO — that is our business, not theirs. No flattery templates, no fake familiarity, never promise payment or links in return.

WHAT WE KNOW ABOUT THE BUSINESS (use only these facts; put [brackets] around anything the owner must fill in)
{{ $json.facts }}
Our pages: {{ ($json.our_pages || []).join(', ') || 'https://' + $json.domain + '/' }}

PAGES (quote something from the page itself in the first sentence — its title or the question it answers; never say how we found it)
{{ ($json.jobs || []).map(j => j.n + '. [' + j.kind + ' / ' + j.action_type + '] ' + j.url + (j.title ? ' — "' + j.title + '"' : '') + '\n   the question their readers ask: "' + j.question + '"' + (j.competitors_named.length ? '\n   It names: ' + j.competitors_named.join(', ') + ' (not us)' : '') + (j.kind === 'correction' ? '\n   CORRECTION: the page says "' + j.claim + '" about us. The fact on file: "' + j.true_fact + '"' : '')).join('\n') }}

How to write each:
- list (a "best / top providers" list): to the editor. One sentence on why {{ $json.business }} belongs on this list for its readers, then the facts they would need (what we do, for whom, where, one proof point from the facts). Offer to send a logo or a short description.
- article / news: to the author. Offer something useful for the piece: an expert quote (in [brackets] for the owner to confirm), a data point from the facts, or a correction/update. Name the article.
- reply (a forum or community thread): write the REPLY itself, not an e-mail. Helpful first — answer the thread's question in 60-110 words with practical advice — and disclose plainly "I work for {{ $json.business }}"; mention the business once, no link unless it directly answers the question.

- correction (the page states something wrong about {{ $json.business }}): to the author or editor. Name the page, say politely which statement is out of date or inaccurate (quote it), give ONLY the fact written after "The fact on file" as the correct statement and offer to send proof [Owner: attach a source that shows it]. Never add any other fact, number or date; never mention AI. One clear ask: please update that line.

Rules: e-mails have a subject under 60 characters and a 70-120 word plain-text body signed "[Your name], {{ $json.business }}"; replies have an empty subject. Write the business name exactly as it stands above, every time (never the website address). The first sentence quotes or names something on their page. One clear ask per e-mail. Never invent clients, numbers, awards, accreditations or certifications — anything the facts above do not carry goes in as [Owner: confirm — …]; never claim facts about their page you were not given.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"drafts": [{"n": 1, "subject": "", "body": ""}]}

parameters.content:
## SEO Agent — AI Growth (v4.12, AI_GROWTH_SPEC.md)
**Once a week in each website's own cycle** (job 5: after the AI Visibility Tracker and the Site Tracker, before the Content Cadence; *Manual Run* `{ trigger: 'cycle', domain, site_id, cycle_key, job, monthly, scheduled_for, request_id }`; the Wikidata check only when `monthly: true`) and on demand (*Manual Run* `{{ domain | site_id, email?, callback_url? }}`). Per site with AI visibility and `ai_growth` on (`seo_monitors`; default on): the work that gets the business **named and cited** in AI answers.
**Indexing**: new / updated pages and key pages Bing has not crawled → **Bing Webmaster Tools SubmitUrlBatch** (the index **Bing and Microsoft Copilot** answer from; OpenAI documents OAI-SearchBot, not Bing, for ChatGPT search; key SEO_BING_WEBMASTER_API_KEY: on) and **IndexNow** once the site hosts its key file (`seo_cache` `indexnow:`; Bing, Yandex, Naver, Seznam, Yep — not Google, and a submission "does not guarantee immediate indexing"). **B9-2**: every page sent in the last 45 days is asked about again (GetUrlInfo) and the report says how many Bing has **since crawled** — measured, or "not available" with the reason. **B9-3**: `robots.txt` is read first (*Robots Verdicts (Growth)*) and judged per page for OAI-SearchBot / ChatGPT-User / PerplexityBot / Claude-SearchBot / Googlebot / Bingbot — a page no AI fetcher may read gets **no readiness score** and is not submitted. **AI readiness** of up to 12 key pages a week (`seo_ai_pages`): raw HTML without JavaScript, answer in the first ~200 characters, visible update date ≤ 90 days, question headings, sourced figures, lists, author; Bing's crawl state (GetUrlInfo).
**Questions to win** (`seo_ai_targets`): every lost question of the latest AI visibility run → a new answer page or a refresh of the page the site has; the **Content Cadence** writes the queued ones (`ai_pages_month`, default 2) with the question, the AI's searches and its sources. **B9-4**: a target is **won** only when at least 2 answers of the last 8 days (weekly + pulse) named the business, with the count printed — and a won question that is lost again goes back in the queue with both dates and an alert. **B9-5**: a page AI cited in earlier weekly checks and in neither of the last two is raised as a refresh, with the counts. **Earned media**: the exact third-party pages AI cited in answers that did not name the business, fetched (do they name you / your competitors?), one action per kind, drafts for the 3 most valuable (*AI Outreach Writer*), kept as prospects (`seo_link_prospects` ai_source) for the Backlink Monitor's contacts and follow-ups. **Entity**: Wikidata monthly. Run row → `seo_ai_growth`; report e-mail + callback `ai_growth`. Cost: Claude for the drafts (~$0.03 a site); everything else is free.
